S33.01.needs: a signed-in account with at least one published artifact
S33.01.note: The exact web settings nav label for this section was not found as text; the Desktop cloud settings modal labels the same section Shared links (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/DesktopCloudSettingsModal.tsx). The row shows no explicit state label beyond the audience and the Published date.
steps: Sign in, open Settings and choose Shared links.
Scroll below the shared conversation links to the Published artifacts heading.
Look at each row: title, audience (Anyone with the link, Everyone in this workspace or Only people you invite), kind, size, Published date.
Check the row buttons Open, History and Unpublish, and the empty text No published artifacts when there are none.

S33.04.note: The prompt-to-artifact step itself was not traced in the listed files; only the Publish step was confirmed.
steps: Sign in, open a new chat and type a prompt asking the assistant to build a small web page.
Wait for the artifact panel to show the generated page.
Click Publish in the artifact panel.
Look for the toast Published · link copied to clipboard, and confirm the page is now hosted at a link.
S33.04.where: Chat > ask the assistant for a web page or app > artifact panel > Publish

labels.text: Published. Copy the link from the bar below.

S33.07.note: The code calls the result a public link or shareUrl; no separate preview deployment control was found, so this is the same Publish action as S33.04.
steps: Open an artifact that the assistant created in a chat.
Click Publish in the artifact panel.
Wait for the toast and copy the link from the bar below if the clipboard was not used.
Open the link in a new private window and compare with Expected.

S33.10.needs: a signed-in account and a private browser window
S33.10.note: The public page is served from the shared-artifact route; the exact on-screen text of the page itself was not traced.
steps: Publish an artifact from the artifact panel.
Copy the link from the toast or from the bar below.
Open the link in a new private window with no sign-in.
Compare the page you see with Expected; also check that Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts lists it with Open.
S33.10.where: Chat > artifact panel > Publish, then Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts > Open

S33.12.needs: a workspace with a second member account
S33.12.note: The workspace option only appears in the audience menu when the member count is known, and the exact text there is built with the count in brackets.
steps: Open a published artifact in the artifact panel and open its audience menu (the select next to Publish).
Choose Everyone in this workspace.
Open the link in a private window with no sign-in and check that it does not open.
Sign in as a second member of the same workspace and open the link to compare with Expected.
S33.12.where: Chat > artifact panel > Publish > audience menu > Everyone in this workspace

S33.23.needs: a published artifact with at least two published versions
S33.23.note: The chat artifact menu also has Restore version N, but that restores an earlier local version in the editor, not the live site.
steps: Publish an artifact, edit it in chat and publish again so it has two versions.
Open Settings > Shared links, find the artifact under Published artifacts and click History.
Pick an earlier version and click Put live.
Open the public link and look for the earlier content, and for the text Version N of ... is live again.
S33.23.where: Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts > History > Put live

steps: Open Settings > Shared links and find the artifact under Published artifacts.
Click Unpublish on its row.
In the dialog Unpublish this artifact?, read the warning and click Unpublish artifact to confirm, or Cancel to stop.
Open the public link and check that it no longer works, and that the row disappears or shows the notice Unpublished.
S33.24.where: Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts > Unpublish

labels.text: Duplicated. Edits here no longer touch the original.

S33.25.note: The button that opens this menu was not identified by its visible text; the menu item and toast were confirmed.
steps: Open an artifact in the artifact panel.
Open the artifact's menu and click Duplicate.
Look for the toast Duplicated. Edits here no longer touch the original.
Edit the copy and check that the original artifact is unchanged.

S33.26.note: The source item label is built from the artifact language, so the extension in the menu text varies.
steps: Open an artifact in the artifact panel.
Click Download.
Choose Download source (.html) or the extension that matches the artifact language.
Open the saved file and compare its content with the artifact source.
S33.26.where: Chat > artifact panel > Download > Download source

S33.28.needs: a published link opened in a browser
S33.28.note: The visible report link covers infringement or impersonation only; no general abuse option was found on the page itself.
steps: Open a published artifact link in a browser window.
Scroll to the bottom of the page.
Click Report infringement or impersonation.
Check that the copyright report form opens for this page.
S33.28.where: Open a published link (Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts > Open) > scroll to the bottom > Report infringement or impersonation

S33.29.note: The moderation check and its refusal message were found in the server routes (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts), but no exact error text was confirmed, so the tester may not be able to trigger it.
steps: Publish an artifact from the artifact panel.
If the server refuses the publication, look for an error message instead of the success toast Published.
Compare with Expected: a site that is refused or taken down should not stay public.
S33.29.where: Effect is seen when publishing from the artifact panel (Chat > artifact panel > Publish); the moderation check runs on the server.

S33.30.needs: a published artifact with saved visitor data, if you want to see that data removed
S33.30.note: No separate delete-app control was found; the only removal is Unpublish, which the dialog says deletes visitor data. Deleting a chat also unpublishes its artifacts in apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts, but the chat delete button label was not searched.
steps: Open Settings > Shared links and find the artifact under Published artifacts.
Click Unpublish and read the dialog text about the data the site saved for its visitors.
Click Unpublish artifact to confirm.
Check that the row is gone and the public link no longer works.
S33.30.where: Settings > Shared links > Published artifacts > Unpublish > Unpublish artifact
